# v1 alpha: close the gap

Local only, never PR it. Written 2026-11-17 from three Codex reports (`docs/research/2026-11-17-*.json`, untracked), the Codex adversarial audit (`/tmp/callisto-adversarial-audit-2026-11-17/`), the Changesets v3 announcement, migration and automation guides, e18e's publishing guide, and three read-only verification lanes at `ab3c030`. Every finding below was confirmed in source (file:line); the load-bearing ones were re-read by hand. Nothing was built or changed.

## Root causes, not findings

Twenty findings reduce to seven model flaws. Fix the flaw and the findings cannot come back; patch the findings and they will.

| # | Flaw | Findings it produces | Structural fix (first rung that works) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| R1 | "Is there releasable input" is not a value. Each consumer rebuilds it from a stand-in: the winning `named_by`, a count of resolvable changeset files, `consumed` being empty, a deleted `.md` in the merged diff | F02 retained prerelease note erases fresh inference (`aggregate.rs:325-392`, also drops group and dependent bumps); F03 invalid notes become a green no-op (`release_pr.rs:112`, script `:78-81`); inferred-only changes never open a release PR; pre-mode decide loop (retained notes keep `has_changesets` true forever); E165 `NoChangesetConsumed` (`release_decision.rs:483`); `version.rs:351-359` empty check; `InferredReleaseWithoutChangeset` warning; dead `CascadeInput.named_by` (`cascade.rs:137`); `reason_from_bump` maps `None` to `Changeset` (`release_decision.rs:957`) | `Seed { severity, sources: NonEmpty<Source> }`, `enum Source { FreshChangeset, RetainedChangeset, Inference, Group }`; severity is the max, "fresh" is an exhaustive match. `ReleasePrDecisionV2::derive` takes a `PendingRelease` with a private constructor built only from a strictly loaded `VersionPlan`; the `bool` goes. The decision records `consumed_changesets`, so E165 compares sets |
| R2 | Native identity is a raw `String`; normalization is free helpers some callers apply | F01 high: PEP 503-equivalent PyPI names admitted as two owners (`walk.rs:298`), one upload, both tags. Sibling: crates.io `-`/`_`/case (`package_id.rs:189`). Selector `pypi/my-pkg` gets E102 while dependency resolution matches (`identity.rs:404`). Config rules, tags, `add` compare raw | `NativeName` in `callisto-model::identity`: private field, `new(Ecosystem, &str)`, keeps display spelling, `Eq/Hash/Ord` on the canonical key (PyPI PEP 503, Cargo lowercase with `_`->`-`, npm exact). `native_owner`, `IdentityIndex.native`, `ReleasePackageId.name`, config rule matching key on it |
| R3 | Values lose structure at boundaries: refs, YAML scalars, HTTP framing, input origin travel as `&str` | F04 `last_ref_segment` takes the last `/` (`init.rs:734`, two callers); F05 seven raw `replace()` into YAML (`init.rs:902-909`), `__COMMIT__` never parsed as `CommitSha`; F06 `rsplit_once("\r\n\r\n")` truncates a body with a blank line (`http.rs:56`; fails loudly); F10 every JSON parse error is E281/usage and paths ignore `--cwd` (`io.rs:19`); `checkpoint.rs` trailer search, `ls-tree` without `-z` | `BranchName` (only `from_full_ref` or `git check-ref-format --branch`); one `WorkflowScalar` encoder that `render_workflow` requires by type; header-first HTTP parse; `enum JsonInput { Stdin, Inline, File(PathBuf) }` through `resolve_file_arg` |
| R4 | One resolution, two implementations, no index | F07 O(E x P) relative `workspace:` lookup (`walk.rs:34-68,776`; 12x at 800 packages); `npm.rs:92-113` resolves the same path again and swallows errors | Canonical-dir -> `PackageId` index built once; both callers use it |
| R5 | Checks that cannot fail | F08 `! cargo tree | grep` passes when cargo fails (`justfile:99,111`); `coverage-per-crate` passes on empty data; bench prints "failed" and exits 0; flaky graph test is fixture portability (bsdtar `._*` with xattrs, bare `cargo` from PATH) | Boundaries move into `deny.toml`; `set shell := ["bash", "-euo", "pipefail", "-c"]`; bench exits 1; fixture uses `$CARGO` and `COPYFILE_DISABLE=1` |
| R6 | Wire compatibility assumed, not modeled | v3 `pre.json` (`{mode, tag}`) fails to parse (`pre.rs:106-133`); callisto writes v2 only, drops unknown keys; `.changeset/pre/` ignored and a move there fails E165 `UnexpectedPath`; ADR 1 says "same shape" | `enum PreStateShape { V2, V3 }` read from the file, written back in the shape read. Retained notes become `Source::RetainedChangeset` whichever shape stored them |
| R7 | Publish credentials and untrusted code share a process or job | Simple template: one `release` job builds and publishes with `id-token: write`; matrix `build` job runs project build code with `id-token: write` (for attestations); npm publish runs from the source directory, so lifecycle scripts run inside the process that holds npm's OIDC variables | Pack, then publish the tarball with `--ignore-scripts` in a job that runs no project code; attestation in its own job over uploaded artifacts; `id-token` only on that job and the publish job |

R1 and R6 meet: v3's split (root = fresh, `pre/` = retained) is the fresh/retained distinction R1 introduces. Build `Source` first; v3 support is then mostly storage. R7 must land before OIDC: with trusted publishing, a job holding `id-token` that runs build code can mint a publish token, because npm's trust is per workflow file unless bound to an environment, and this repo's policy forbids environments.

## Changesets v3: what changed and where Callisto stands

| v3 change | Callisto today | Action |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Peer dependents get a patch, not a major; authors add an explicit major when needed | Out-of-range peer + minor/major source -> Major when `peer-escalation = true`, the default (`cascade.rs:46-52`). That is v2's behaviour | Flip the default to `false` (the dependent then gets `cascade.bump-severity`, patch). Owner decision; a default change ships as **Breaking** |
| Dev-dependency ranges rewritten without releasing the owner | Cascade never follows dev edges; an unrewritable dev range is left with a warning (`cascade.rs:437,612`) | Add the scenario test (a 1.0.0->2.0.0, b dev `^1`): range rewritten, b not released |
| Build, pack, publish as separate jobs; `id-token` only on publish (e18e standard workflow) | Matrix: separate `build` and `execute`, but `build` holds `id-token`. Simple: one job | R7 (WP L) |
| Pre mode: consumed notes move to `.changeset/pre/`, `pre.json` drops ids, auto-migrates on `status` | v2 shape only; v3 repos fail | R6 (WP G). Read both, write the shape read; no silent migration |
| `changeset status --since=<ref>` exits 1 when changed packages lack changesets; `changeset --empty` | No equivalent; `status --check` gates errors only | WP M: one diagnostic in `status` over changed packages, gated by an existing exit path. New flag only with owner confirmation |
| `version` exits 1 with no unreleased changesets | No changesets is an error only under `--strict` | Keep. Callisto's `release-pr decide` is the automation entry point, so a script never runs `version` blind |
| `add --major/--minor/--patch --message` | `add --package <id>:<bump> --summary` already non-interactive | None |
| Private packages not versioned or tagged by default (`privatePackages`) | Private npm workspace root skipped; other private packages versioned | Check and document in the migration page; change only if a user hits it |
| `baseBranch` defaults to `main`; `tag` renamed `git-tag`; `access: private` -> `restricted` | `init` ignores `baseBranch` and `access` with a warning | Migration (WP K) |
| Changelog formatting through the project's formatter (prettier, oxfmt, deno, dprint) | Callisto renders its own Markdown | None |
| Staged npm publishing | Not supported; v3 does not support it either | Defer; separate decision |
| Release PR through a GitHub App token so CI runs on it | Action takes a token input (not checked) | Check in WP L; document |

## Map to the gap analysis

The positioning is "reviewable, dependency-aware releases with recovery from partial failures". F01 (a wrong `alreadySatisfied` adoption), F02 and F03 (silent omissions) sit inside that claim, so they come before any evidence is published.

| Gap | Covered by |
| --- | --- |
| 1 Tokenless publishing | L, J; real proof in R |
| 2 Managed prerelease | F1, F2, G, H |
| 3 Inferred-only release PRs | F1, F2 |
| 4 Contributor coverage check | M |
| 5 Changesets v2/v3 migration | G, K, N |
| 6 Python fit (co-located Maturin, private/HTML PyPI) | Out of alpha scope (after v1) |
| 7 Windows, other forges | Out of alpha scope |
| 8 Readiness evidence (recovery, registry binding, native matrix, onboarding) | Q, R |
| Recovery and integrity defects found since | E (F01), F1/F2 (F02, F03), B (F06) |
| Rust evaluation (unused `tracing`, `homepage`) | A |
| External validation (five owners, Sampo head-to-head) | After H and Q; owner-run |

## Product gaps from the landscape research

- Managed prerelease: owner said yes (crucial for our own releases). Unblocked by R1 + R6; then delete `reject_pre_mode` and E318.
- Inferred-only release PRs: falls out of R1 (`PendingRelease` from the post-cascade plan). Opt-in per package through the existing `release-trigger`; no new key. ADR 2 does not forbid it; its consequence bullet and specs `release.json:368`, `cli.json:191` change.
- OIDC through native tools, after R7: add `twine` + `ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_*` to `credentials_needed_by` (`runner.rs:82`); `PYPI_TOKEN` optional in init; a pinned `crates-io-auth-action` step feeding `CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN`; fix `OIDC-TRUSTED-PUBLISHING.md` lines 21, 22, 24. No config key. Tokenless publish stays unproven until run against real registries.
- Changesets v2 and v3 migration: R6, then `init` translation of `linked`/`ignore`/`access`/`baseBranch` where an equivalent exists, and a page listing semantic differences (linked groups bump every live member; peer policy; private packages).
- Hygiene: delete workspace `tracing`; drop `homepage` (equal to `repository`; Cargo 1.100 warns).

## Pushback

- No Tokio, plugin framework, trait-per-concern rewrite or execution journal. Every finding is a lost value, a duplicated rule or a shared trust boundary: a type, an index or a job split fixes each.
- e18e recommends a protected GitHub Environment with required reviewers. This repo's policy forbids it; R7 gets most of the benefit by keeping `id-token` off every job that runs project code. Binding trusted publishers to an environment stays the owner's call.
- No unwrap lint move: measured 806 errors in integration-test helpers; the `justfile` shape works.
- No toolchain pin yet: CI's toolchain comes from `orin-dx/actions/setup-rust` (not read). Locally `stable` is 1.98.1, a session override pins 1.99.1, 1.100.0 is current; clippy is clean on 1.100.0.
- F06 is lower than the audit's medium: it fails loudly, only with pretty-printed bodies.
- No plan-comparison command for migration until its value is measured.
- "No ceremony" keeps what the ruleset enforces: signed commits, trails, changesets for released-behaviour fixes, exit-code gates.
- AGENTS.md forbids parallel cargo builds. Swarm parallelism is in reading, design and editing; builds take one machine-wide lock. Relaxing that is the owner's call.

## Work packages

Changeset = fix to released behaviour or a default change.

| WP | Scope | Files (overlap risk) | Changeset | Model / effort |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A | R5 gates + hygiene | `justfile`, `deny.toml`, `Cargo.toml`, bench, `provider/registry/tests.rs` | no | Sonnet, medium |
| B | F06 HTTP parser | `provider/http.rs` | yes | Sonnet, medium |
| C | F10 typed JSON input | `cli/io.rs`, `cli/commands/release_pr.rs` (args only) | yes | Sonnet, medium |
| D | R3 init boundary: `BranchName`, `WorkflowScalar`, `CommitSha` for `__COMMIT__`, F09 hint and E278 help | `graph/commands/init.rs`, templates, `cli/commands/init.rs` | yes | Opus, medium |
| E | R2 `NativeName` | `model/identity.rs`, `package_id.rs`, `walk.rs` admission, `identity.rs`, `config/resolve.rs`, `tags.rs`, `release_decision.rs:28-44` | yes | Opus, high |
| F1 | R1 `Seed`/`Source` in aggregation | `aggregate.rs`, `cascade.rs`, `version.rs`, `status.rs` | yes (F02) | Opus, high |
| F2 | R1 `PendingRelease`, decision `consumed_changesets`, E165 sets; inferred release PRs; F03 | `model/release_pr.rs`, `cli/commands/release_pr.rs`, `release_decision.rs`, `model/release/decision.rs`, action script, ADR 2, specs, `wire-compat.md` | yes | Opus, high |
| G | R6 `pre.json` v2/v3 + `pre/` archive | `model/format/pre.rs`, `aggregate.rs` listing, `release_decision.rs` allowed paths, ADR 1 | yes | Opus, medium |
| H | Managed prerelease: delete E318, release-PR loop over a pre cycle, lifecycle test | `cli/commands/release_pr.rs`, action script, specs, `errors.md` | yes | Opus, high |
| I | R4 dir index (F07) + pnpm-relative bench shape | `walk.rs` edges, `manifests/npm.rs`, `fixtures/perf.rs` | yes | Sonnet, high |
| L | R7 publish isolation: pack then publish tarball with `--ignore-scripts`; simple template split into build and publish jobs; attestation job; `id-token` only where needed | `registry_argv.rs`, npm provider, templates, `init.rs`, this repo's release workflow + policy script | yes | Opus, high |
| J | OIDC native (after L) | `cli/runner.rs`, init templates, docs | yes | Sonnet, medium |
| K | Migration v2/v3: init translation + docs | `graph/commands/init.rs` key table, docs | yes | Sonnet, medium |
| M | Changed-without-changeset check (v3 `status --since`) | `status.rs`, `cli.rs` | yes | Sonnet, medium |
| N | Peer default to v3 policy + dev-edge scenario test | `config` defaults, `docs/config.md`, cascade tests | yes (Breaking) | Sonnet, medium |

| Q | Recovery evidence, the positioning claim: a local `just verify-real` harness against local registries (npm verdaccio-style, `cargo-http-registry`, a local PyPI) rehearsing partial publish -> rerun adopts, delayed visibility, conflicting tag, missing Python artifact; production registry binding for Cargo/PyPI (`registry_endpoint.rs` rejects non-https loopback, so the harness needs a test-only allowance decided first); the native install/load matrix recorded from `native_resolution_e2e_tests` | `registry_endpoint.rs`, new harness, docs | no | Opus, high |
| R | Onboarding time and tokenless publish against real registries | needs owner accounts | no | owner + Sonnet |

Investigations (read-only, any time): GH token stripped from native git vs `gh auth git-credential` (needs a clean Linux runner); process-tree cancellation and unbounded output in `run`; multi-distribution prerequisite edges; Sampo head-to-head on one mixed workspace after H.

## Waves

- Wave 0 (now, disjoint files): A, B, C.
- Wave 1: D, E, F1. E and F1 both touch `release_decision.rs` at different ranges: `git merge-tree` before the second merges.
- Wave 2 (critical path, serial): F2 -> G -> H. In parallel: I (after E, shares `walk.rs`), L (after D, shares templates and `init.rs`), N.
- Wave 3: J (after L), K (after G), M (after F2, shares `status.rs`), Q (after E and F2, so it rehearses the fixed model).
- Wave 4: R, then the external pilot.

Critical path: F1 -> F2 -> G -> H. Second chain: D -> L -> J.

## How the swarm runs

- One named worktree per WP, branch off `main`, no stacks; merge in wave order.
- Builds: each worktree has its own target dir; every cargo invocation takes one machine-wide lock (`flock $TMPDIR/callisto-cargo.lock cargo ...`), so agents overlap on thinking and editing, never on builds.
- Per WP: the implementer writes the regression first, driving the real binary or function at the boundary named in the finding, then the type change, then deletes checks the type now covers.
- Proof by exit code: `just pre-push && just lint && just doc-check && just test`; `cargo mutants --in-diff` on the WP diff with zero missed except argued equivalents (it found two real gaps on a caliper branch today); sibling sweep listed in the PR body.
- Review: one fresh-context Opus reviewer per WP, given the diff and the finding, not the implementer's reasoning.
- Gates run unsandboxed in the worktree: sandboxed runs fail tests that write inside the repo and look like defects.
- Ship: signed commit, changeset via `callisto add`, push, link a trail (#357 for A-E, I; #250 or a new prerelease trail for F-H, K, M, N; a new publish-security trail for L, J).
- Orchestration: a Workflow script can run each wave as a pipeline (implement -> mutate -> review -> gate), with the build lock as the only shared resource; it needs an explicit "use a workflow".

## Alpha scope (planning only, not documented)

GitHub-hosted, Linux/macOS, Cargo + npm (napi-rs included), separate-directory Python. Out: Windows, other forges, co-located Maturin, private/HTML PyPI, staged npm publish.

## Settled decisions

Decided; sessions do not ask.

1. ADR 2's consequence bullet amended: inferred-only release PRs allowed through `release-trigger`.
2. Decision schema v3 with `consumed_changesets`; readers accept 1-3.
3. `pre.json` written back in the shape read.
4. Cargo `foo-bar`/`foo_bar` in one workspace is E100.
5. `init --workflow` adds the workflow when `callisto.toml` exists.
6. OIDC before 1.0, after R7, with `id-token: write` on this repo's `execute` job.
7. Peer default moves to v3's patch policy, shipped as Breaking.
8. One changed-without-changeset flag on `status`.
9. Builds run in parallel across worktrees (each has its own `target/`); never two in one worktree. WP A rewords AGENTS.md's "Never run cargo builds in parallel" to say "in the same checkout".

## Where the owner is needed

- Launching the sessions.
- Merging PRs (sessions never merge), in wave order.
- Registry accounts for R (tokenless publish, onboarding time) and the external pilot.
# v1 alpha: session launch prompts

Local only. Plan: `.claude/plans/PLAN-v1-alpha-close-the-gap.md`. Open each session in `/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto`, set model and effort, paste the prompt. Sessions run unattended; they come back to you only to merge.

| Session | Work | `/model` | `/effort` |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 Release model | F1 -> F2 -> G -> H -> M | Opus 5.5 | medium |
| 2 Publish chain | D -> L -> J | Sonnet 5.5 | medium |
| 3 Fixes | A, B, C (workflow), then K (after G merges) and N | Sonnet 5.5 | medium |
| 5 Identity and graph | E -> I | Sonnet 5.5 | medium |
| 4 Evidence (after E and F2 merge) | Q | Sonnet 5.5 | medium |

Opus spend is limited to Session 1 (one cross-cutting semantic change, where a rework loop costs more than Opus) and to subagents: an Opus design note at the start of L, E and Q, and the Opus reviewer per PR.

Capacity: disk is the limit (about 98 GB free; stale worktree `target/` dirs hold about 89 GB, all regenerable). With debug info off, expect a few GB per active worktree. Sessions 1, 3 (three Wave 0 worktrees) and 5 build at once from the start; Session 2 starts with them because J's first change is tiny, and its heavier builds overlap Wave 0 finishing.

Before launch, free the stale build output (build artifacts only, no source or branches touched):

```
cd ~/Projects/callisto && rm -rf .claude/worktrees/*/target
```

Launch all from a shell in the repo (each prints an id; `claude agents` lists them, `claude attach <id>` watches one):

```
cd ~/Projects/callisto
claude --bg --model opus   --effort medium "Run Session 1 in .claude/plans/LAUNCH-v1-alpha-sessions.md."
claude --bg --model sonnet --effort medium "Run Session 2 in .claude/plans/LAUNCH-v1-alpha-sessions.md."
claude --bg --model sonnet --effort medium "Use a workflow: run Session 3 in .claude/plans/LAUNCH-v1-alpha-sessions.md."
claude --bg --model sonnet --effort medium "Run Session 5 in .claude/plans/LAUNCH-v1-alpha-sessions.md."
# after E and F2 merge:
claude --bg --model sonnet --effort medium "Run Session 4 in .claude/plans/LAUNCH-v1-alpha-sessions.md."
```

## Session 1

Done when: generated workflows carry any valid branch name exactly in both templates; no job that runs project code holds id-token or registry credentials; npm-family publishes a packed tarball with --ignore-scripts; twine and crates.io can publish with no token through native OIDC (unproven against real registries until I run it).

Use a workflow for work packages A, B and C from .claude/plans/PLAN-v1-alpha-close-the-gap.md: one worktree and PR each, pipeline implement (sonnet) -> mutants -> fresh review (opus) -> gate, under 10 agents, cargo lock shared. Trail #357.

== callisto/173
- medium None None |  | The workflow-only path accepts existing artifact configurations without checking whether the generated builder supports their owners. For example, an npm-owned artifact passes config resolution, but `commands/matrix.rs:58` excludes it and the matrix workflow's slot lookup then fails with `callisto matrix has no entry for artifact slot`, blocking releases. Validate existing artifact owners against the supported Cargo binary builder before writing the workflow.
- medium None None |  | For the valid Git branch name `__BRANCH__`, `render_workflow` first inserts `"__BRANCH__"` into the trigger, then replaces that inserted placeholder again, producing `branches: [""__BRANCH__""]`. This newly makes the generated YAML invalid; substitute placeholders in one pass without processing inserted values.

Some further context from codex:



<pasted_content id="cd46">
Callisto is partially aligned with the e18e publishing guide (https://e18e.dev/docs/publishing.html). The largest gaps are npm build/publish isolation, token-first setup guidance, and staged publishing. Our decision to delegate authentication to native tools remains sound.

I inspected the current checkout, generated workflows, npm adapter, credential handling, and live repository rules. Callisto itself currently distributes through Cargo and GitHub Releases; it has no tracked npm package. The npm assessment therefore concerns the publishing service we provide to users.

| Area | Assessment | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| Pinned actions | Aligned | Generated workflows use full commit SHAs; our repository has Dependabot for actions. |
| Restricted permissions | Partially aligned | Permissions are job-scoped, but generated publishing jobs also need repository writes for tags. |
| Native OIDC | Compatible, poorly documented | The runner preserves npm’s GitHub OIDC inputs, and token configuration is conditional. Our setup documentation describes tokens rather than a complete tokenless path. |
| Provenance | Partially aligned | Generated workflows request npm provenance. This does not establish that execution uploads a previously verified npm archive. |
| Build/publish separation | Significant gap | npm publishes a workspace/directory and can execute publishing hooks. We do not transport a sealed npm tarball from an isolated build. |
| Disabled lifecycle scripts | Deliberate difference | Publishing hooks explicitly retain their normal behavior. |
| npm staging | Unsupported | We invoke direct publishing and have no staged-submission lifecycle. |
| Package validation | Missing integration | Generated workflows do not run publint or validate packed npm contents. |
| Review protection | Partially aligned | Live main rules require one review and dismiss stale approvals, but latest-push approval is disabled and bypass actors exist. |
| Immutable releases | Not currently demonstrated | The latest release, callisto@0.21.1, reports immutable: false. |

The most useful changes are the following.

1. Make “build once, publish those exact bytes” available for npm.

The npm adapter currently ignores its artifact-manifest argument and publishes from the checkout. That allows prepublishOnly, prepack, and other native hooks to execute with publishing authority. This is documented behavior, so silently disabling hooks would break our existing contract. See npm adapter (crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/release/provider/registry/npm.rs:197) and publishing-hook policy (docs/releasing.md:64).

I recommend an explicit prepacked publishing route:

- Build and pack without npm publishing authority.
- Use the appropriate native packer so workspace dependency transformations remain correct.
- Validate the packed package’s identity, version, contents and dependency references; run publint there.
- Record the archive’s digest in our existing artifact contract.
- Upload that verified archive without rebuilding or running package hooks.

This fits our current architecture. It needs an npm artifact model and adapter support, not a new execution framework.

2. Treat OIDC permission as publishing authority—even without an npm token.

Our generated matrix build job has id-token: write for attestations. If an npm package trusts that same workflow without an environment restriction, build code can also request credentials for npm publication. Keeping NPM_TOKEN out of the build job does not isolate that authority. This is conditional on the package’s trusted-publisher configuration; I did not attempt a live token exchange. See matrix permissions (crates/callisto-graph/src/templates/matrix_workflow.tmpl:101) and npm’s trust configuration (https://docs.npmjs.com/trusted-publishers/).

For generated npm workflows, we need a deliberate trust boundary: for example, a customer-configured environment restriction or a separate publishing workflow identity. A branch if: condition alone is insufficient when a writer can modify the workflow on another branch.

Our own repository explicitly forbids GitHub Environment/reviewer gates. I have preserved that policy. The guide identifies a tradeoff to document and address in customer workflows; it does not authorize changing our release approval model.

3. Improve OIDC setup while continuing to let npm own authentication.

The existing runner largely gets out of npm’s way. The action only creates token configuration when NPM_TOKEN is nonempty. Those are useful foundations.

The missing work is operational:

- Document tokenless trusted publishing as a first-class path.
- Generate a tested Node/npm setup instead of relying on the runner image.
- Keep token authentication available for unsupported providers and registries.
- Explain separate read authentication for private dependencies and registry observations.

Current npm documentation requires npm 11.5.1+ and Node 22.14+ for trusted publishing, while staging requires npm 11.15+. We should test an explicit toolchain combination. We do not need to implement token exchange ourselves. Trusted publishing (https://docs.npmjs.com/trusted-publishers/), staging requirements (https://docs.npmjs.com/staged-publishing/).

Our publishing documentation (docs/publishing.md:42) currently presents two token patterns and a Node 20 example; it needs a distinct modern OIDC recipe.

4. Staging needs a separate completion model.

e18e recommends submitting packages with npm stage publish, followed by maintainer approval. A staged package is not yet publicly available. npm staged publishing (https://docs.npmjs.com/staged-publishing/).

Simply changing our command would be incorrect. Callisto currently waits for public registry visibility before completing publication and permitting announcements. A staged submission could succeed, then our confirmation window would expire while it awaits human approval.

Proper support must distinguish:

- Submitted for approval.
- Publicly published.
- Rejected or conflicting submission.

It also needs rerun handling for versions already staged. npm’s OIDC credentials cannot perform stage inspection or approval, which constrains reconciliation. Approval should remain with npm and the maintainer. This deserves a focused design before adding a staging flag.

5. Tighten the supporting practices without making everything a release gate.

publint belongs in a configurable, credential-free validation step. Account 2FA, npm trusted-publisher permissions and organization Actions restrictions need operator guidance; I could not verify those account-level settings.

The live main ruleset (https://github.com/orin-dx/callisto/rules/22292852) and mutable latest release also differ from the guide’s stricter recommendations. Whether to tighten bypasses, require latest-push approval, or enable immutable stable releases is an owner policy decision.

One caution about copying examples: e18e’s standard template (https://github.com/e18e/setup-publish/blob/main/templates/default.yml) separates packing and stages a tarball, but its linked Changesets template (https://github.com/e18e/setup-publish/blob/main/templates/changesets.yml) builds in the publishing job and does not explicitly invoke staging. The templates themselves provide different guarantees.

My priority order is OIDC documentation/toolchain setup, publishing-authority isolation, verified npm archives, then optional staging support. Native authentication should stay native; Callisto should own the artifact and release semantics around it.

Three focused tests passed for publisher arguments, credential routing and descendant credential inheritance. No live publishing or OIDC exchange was attempted, and no files or settings changed.

content.content:
Build-matrix limits:

- An addon crate outside the napi package directory needs a unique crate whose lib name matches `napi.binaryName` (E204).
- Generated `.node` files must be gitignored; release execution requires a clean checkout.
- Cargo `bin` targets build with `cargo build --release --locked`. Other products, such as `cdylib`s, need a manual workflow.
- The napi build and placement roster comes from the release intent, so an unrelated addon does not block a release of another package.
- Native npm lifecycle hooks run unchanged, including any owner-defined publishing or forge effects. Those effects are outside Callisto's release graph.

---

## Release PR and approval

The generated workflow keeps a release PR current. Merging that PR to the protected default branch authorizes publication; Callisto adds no approval step. Require reviews and CI checks in branch protection. A CODEOWNERS file alone does not enforce review.

The action's `version-pr` mode updates the PR; `release` runs `callisto release` for simple workspaces. Artifact and platform packages use plan/build/execute. See the [action inputs](../.github/actions/callisto-action/action.yml).
---
## Where a publish goes

A registry with no `url` in `callisto.toml` publishes wherever the checkout's own configuration says: `.npmrc` for npm and `.cargo/config.toml` for Cargo. Callisto honors that on purpose, so a private registry set there keeps working, and it means those files decide where the registry token is sent. Review changes to them like code. A release pull request cannot carry such a change: a version commit may only touch manifests, lockfiles, changelogs, changesets and the decision file, and any other path fails verification with E165. For npm (except yarn) and PyPI, set `url` on the registry entry to pin the destination in `callisto.toml`; Cargo takes its destination only from `.cargo/config.toml`, and a `url` on a cargo registry is rejected.

---

## npm

Two supported patterns.

### Pattern A: manual `.npmrc` via `NPM_TOKEN`

Set an `NPM_TOKEN` secret. Add this only in the `execute` job, immediately before the publish step:

```yaml
- name: Authenticate with npm registry
  run: npm config set //registry.npmjs.org/:_authToken $NPM_TOKEN
  env:
    NPM_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.NPM_TOKEN }}

- run: callisto release execute --intent "$RUNNER_TEMP/release-intent/release-intent.json" --receipt "$RUNNER_TEMP/release-receipt.json" --orchestration-revision "$GITHUB_SHA"
```

`npm config set` writes the user-level `.npmrc` for later publish calls in the job. The version-PR action receives no token.

The PyPI sibling reproduced and is fixed on #561. The branch is pushed (`git ls-remote` shows `664170d00`) and GitHub reports `valid` for that commit's signature.

- **Reproduction:** with PyPI `foo_bar` beside npm `foo-bar`, then npm removed and the package renamed `foo-bar`, `may_have_held_name_at` returned true. PEP 503 normalization credited the npm tag to the PyPI package. The test failed for PyPI and passed for Cargo before the fix, and covers both ecosystems now.
- **Fix:** one literal-spelling comparison replaces `names_equal` for every ecosystem. A default tag `{name}@` carries the declared spelling, so equivalence never applied to tag ownership.
- **Cleanup:** the PyPI first-word search special case and the now-unused `ecosystem` parameter on `declares` are gone. I rewrote the two earlier history tests to the literal rule.
- **Mutation testing:** I ran `cargo mutants --in-place --in-diff` over `c4fd037a0..HEAD`, which covers `d69bd794e` plus the new commit. 14 mutants: 12 caught, 2 unviable, 0 missed. The earlier `Hash::hash` mutant is outside that diff and is still the one equivalent mutant to note in the PR body.
- **Checks:** `just pre-push`, `just lint`, `just doc-check` and `just test` exited 0 before the commit. The gate was not re-run after the commit. I did not run `just ci`.
- **Shas:**
  - **Fix commit:** `664170d00`.
  - **Earlier Cargo fix:** `d69bd794e`.
  - **Parent:** `23799cdff`.
- **Trailer:** the commits carry no session trailer, per the lead's instruction and the repo rule against session links.

If this matters for the PR body: dropping the PyPI normalization here only affects which tags are credited to which package. Duplicate detection, selectors and `[[package]]` rules still use PEP 503 for PyPI.

lines: +**Large pnpm workspaces load much faster.** Relative `workspace:../path` dependencies are now resolved through one directory index instead of a scan per dependency.
+- At 800 packages with relative `workspace:` paths, `status` drops from about 4.9 s to 0.6 s, `version --dry-run` from 7.6 s to 0.8 s and `release --dry-run` from 6.3 s to 0.9 s.
+- No configuration change is needed. Dependency edges and warnings are unchanged.
+**`release-pr` JSON arguments report where a failure came from.** A relative `--decision` or `--snapshot` file is now read relative to `--cwd`, and a bad file no longer looks like a usage mistake.
+- Malformed inline or stdin JSON is still `E281`, exit 2, naming the flag.
+- A malformed file is `E238`, exit 1, naming the file; an unreadable file is `E213`.
+- `compose-pr-body --preview` follows the same rule: a malformed preview file is `E238`, exit 1, instead of `E281`.
+- **Scripting:** treat exit 1 from a file argument as a data problem, not a bad invocation.
+**Release PRs open for releases inferred from commits.** A package with `release-trigger = "auto"` now gets a release PR from its commits alone; it no longer needs a changeset to be released.
+- `release-pr decide` opens a PR whenever `callisto version` would version a package, after groups and dependents.
+- A changeset that cannot be parsed now fails `release-pr decide` with the error `version` reports, instead of a green run that releases nothing.
+- `status` no longer warns `inferred-release-without-changeset`; that diagnostic code is gone.

+**Scripting:** `version --emit-decision` writes decision schema 3, which adds `consumedChangesets`. Release verification (E165) checks that the release commit deletes exactly those changesets. Schema 1 and 2 decisions still read.

+**Generated release workflows carry any valid branch name.** `callisto init` no longer truncates a default branch such as `release/next` to `next`, and no longer breaks the workflow YAML for branch names containing `,`, `#`, `]` or similar.
+- **Why it matters:** the push trigger and the action `branch` input now name the real default branch, so version PRs target the right base.

+- **Retrying the workflow:** when init skips the workflow (for example, the release tag cannot be resolved), `callisto init --workflow` now adds just the workflow to an initialized workspace and leaves `callisto.toml` untouched. Before, it refused with E190.
+- **Limits:** generated branch names are always double-quoted in the workflow; `+` and `!` are escaped in the trigger filter.
+**Prerelease reruns keep new work.** In a pre cycle, a commit or group change that arrives after a changeset was already applied now releases the next prerelease instead of being dropped.
+- The next prerelease keeps the severity the earlier changeset set, so a major cycle stays `2.0.0-beta.N`.
+- Fixed and linked group members and dependents of such a package are bumped with it.
+- A rerun with nothing new still plans nothing.

18	## Commands

22	- Commits must be signed: the ruleset requires it. Never pass `-c commit.gpgsign=false`. After pushing, `gh api repos/orin-dx/callisto/commits/<sha> --jq .commit.verification.reason` must say `valid`.
23	- Performance: `just bench` times `status`, `version --dry-run` and `release --dry-run` over generated workspaces and counts the git processes each starts (`CALLISTO_BENCH_SHAPES=1` lists which). A change that adds a git process per package fails review.
24	- Scoped iteration: one `cargo test -p <crate>` or `cargo clippy -p <crate> --all-targets -- -D warnings` at a time.
25	  - Not `moon run <project>:test`: its per-project fan-out serializes on `target/`'s build lock.
26	  - Never run cargo builds in parallel in the same checkout.
27	- Never `git checkout -- Cargo.lock` as cleanup. A lockfile diff means investigate, not discard.
28	
29	## Changesets
30	
31	- Write one with `callisto add --package cargo/callisto-cli:<bump> --summary "..."` (non-interactive). Target `callisto-cli`: its changelog is the one users read. One changeset per user-visible topic. A fix to something not yet released has no changeset.
32	- Changesets become the project's changelog, so write them for the people who use it, not for the implementer.
33	- Open with a bold lead-in naming the change as the user sees it, then one line on its value: what they can now do or what changed for them.
34	- When there is more to say, add short bullets in this order: why it matters, how to adopt it (commands, configuration, migration), and limits they will hit. Use sub-bullets for detail.

24	- Scoped iteration: one `cargo test -p <crate>` or `cargo clippy -p <crate> --all-targets -- -D warnings` at a time.
25	  - Not `moon run <project>:test`: its per-project fan-out serializes on `target/`'s build lock.
26	  - Never run cargo builds in parallel in the same checkout.
27	- Never `git checkout -- Cargo.lock` as cleanup. A lockfile diff means investigate, not discard.
28

30	
31	- Write one with `callisto add --package cargo/callisto-cli:<bump> --summary "..."` (non-interactive). Target `callisto-cli`: its changelog is the one users read. One changeset per user-visible topic. A fix to something not yet released has no changeset.
32	- Changesets become the project's changelog, so write them for the people who use it, not for the implementer.
33	- Open with a bold lead-in naming the change as the user sees it, then one line on its value: what they can now do or what changed for them.

WP Q is pushed as PR #572 (trail #460), but `just verify-real` only covers npm and PyPI. Cargo can't be rehearsed.

`just verify-real` exits 0 with 5 of 5 rehearsals passing. `just pre-push`, `just lint`, `just doc-check` and `just test` each exited 0 on the final tree, and so did `just workflow-contracts`. I did not run `just ci`, mutation testing (the diff has no production Rust) or the CI action change on a real runner.

**How it gets past the https rule:** I changed no production code. The local registries serve a self-signed `https://127.0.0.1` certificate, and npm, curl and Twine trust it through their own CA variables. `[registries.npm]` and `[registries.pypi]` therefore bind through the production binding unchanged. The existing test that rejects http, loopback included, still passes.

**What the rehearsals cover:**
- **Partial npm publish:** the registry refuses the second package, then the rerun adopts the first and finishes.
- **PyPI index shows the upload late:** the run waits and succeeds, and the test asserts the index served a 404 first.
- **PyPI index never shows the upload:** the run fails with E157, and a rerun after the index catches up adopts it without re-uploading.
- **Conflicting tag:** the run fails with E167.
- **PyPI index missing one built file:** only the missing wheel is uploaded.

**What it cannot do:**
- **No Cargo rehearsal:** callisto always passes `--registry crates-io`, and cargo sends that publish to the real crates.io API even when the source is replaced. My probe hit crates.io with a fake token and got a 401. Documented in AGENTS.md and `docs/architecture/release.md`. Rehearsing Cargo would take a production change that lets a package name a custom Cargo registry, which is your call.
- **PyPI index is a stand-in:** `pypiserver` can't serve the PEP 691 JSON index that callisto's observation requires. The index side is a small stdlib script over a directory, and `pypiserver` still takes the uploads.
- **Conflicting-tag order:** callisto publishes and tags the dependency package before it reaches the dependent's tag conflict. The test asserts the E167 failure and the untouched foreign tag, not "nothing published".

The native install/load matrix from the plan row is not recorded.

I also moved the shared server helpers into `tests/common/local_registries.rs` and pointed the existing real-registry suite at them. The CI install action now just calls `just verify-real-tools`.

The commit is signed (GitHub reports `valid`) and has no session trailer. The ref `worktree-wp-q-verify-real` matches my local HEAD (`ea17b39a9`) in `git ls-remote`.

I deleted the worktree's `target/`. Once the PR merges, remove the worktree and its local branch.

content.content:
1	**Callisto QA swarm — 18 November 2026**
2	
3	Six new confirmed defects: **one high, four medium and one low**, including one confirmed performance defect. Every finding has an independent validation pass. Final correctness reproductions use a newly built binary from frozen revision `fac8cadf91f792fdd17dec93d36eeb10be24e5f3`.
4	
5	The live checkout advanced from `ab3c030` while discovery ran. I preserved those external merges, archived the newer source into `source-fac8cadf91/`, built it in `current-build/`, and repeated the findings against that binary. Initial discovery and some exploratory optimized benchmarks used the older binary; they are explicitly distinguished below. No implementation changes, commits, pushes or registry/forge effects were made by this audit. All audit artifacts remain outside the public repository.
6	
7	**Complete new finding list**
8	
9	| ID | Severity | Finding | Current source anchor |
10	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
11	| QA-01 | High | Interrupted version recovery can apply a sibling workspace's plan | [checkpoint.rs:198](/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/crates/callisto-model/src/vcs/checkpoint.rs:198) |
12	| QA-02 | Medium | Python requirement rewrites drop epochs and weaken constraints | [python.rs:823](/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/crates/callisto-manifests/src/python.rs:823) |
13	| QA-03 | Medium | Terminal `*` in a package directory selects sibling commits | [access.rs:700](/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/crates/callisto-model/src/vcs/access.rs:700) |
14	| QA-04 | Low | A valid record-separator character in a commit body stops inference | [access.rs:907](/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/crates/callisto-model/src/vcs/access.rs:907) |
15	| QA-05 | Medium | Publication dependencies leak across an owner's native outputs | [derive.rs:503](/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/release/derive.rs:503) |
16	| QA-06 | Medium | Historical ownership checks repeat Git probes for the same commit | [tags.rs:259](/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/crates/callisto-graph/src/tags.rs:259) |
17	
18	Source links point into the live checkout and can move. The immutable inspected copies are under `source-fac8cadf91/` alongside this report.
19	
20	**QA-01 — Recovery can successfully apply the wrong workspace plan. CONFIRMED.**
21	
22	An independent fixture contains sibling directories `  release-work` and `release-work`. The first owns `primary-package`3.4.5 with a patch changeset; the second owns `other-package`3.4.5 with a minor changeset. An ordinary dry run correctly proposes primary3.4.6. The test interrupts the real CLI immediately after successful checkpoint creation, before version writes, then retries.
23	
24	The retry exits0 but reports other-package3.5.0, writes3.5.0 into the primary manifest, consumes the primary patch note, and writes a primary-directory changelog headed `other-package` with the sibling's minor note. The actual sibling remains unchanged. Root reproduced this again on the frozen current binary; `recovery-current/independent-results.json` and `replay.log` contain the before/interruption/after sequence.
25	
26	The first loss is `git_stdout_env` using `stdout_trimmed` for a path. Both the recorded and current workspace prefix lose their leading spaces, so their equality check still passes. `open_checkpoint_tree` then opens the trimmed sibling in the scratch tree. Existing input/version guards can pass because the original files and starting versions match; they do not bind the scratch plan's package roster to the final apply root. ApplyPermit authorizes a write but does not establish that it belongs to the planned workspace.
27	
28	Controls: a normal prefix recovers correctly; missing trimmed sibling refuses E213; a sibling with a different starting version refuses E117. The incorrect success requires the colliding workspace/path/version conditions, not any workspace crash. Leading tabs also fail path recovery. This is a local data-integrity bug; no remote publishing scenario is claimed.
29	
30	Correction direction: preserve native path bytes, removing only the protocol terminator, and verify exact checkpoint/scratch/apply workspace identity plus package roster before mutation. The regression should assert final package identity, version, note consumption and changelog, not only successful retry. Independent report: [recovery validation](validation-recovery/report.md).
31	
32	**QA-02 — Native version data survives the bump but disappears from the requirement. CONFIRMED.**
33	
34	A Python package at `2!0.4.8` patch-releases to `2!0.4.9`. Its co-released dependent's supported `>=2!0.4.8` declaration becomes `>=0.4.9`. The CLI exits0. Independent pip-packaging evaluation proves an epoch-zero version such as99.0.0 was rejected before and accepted after; the old dependency version remains accepted too. An epoch-zero control raises its floor correctly.
35	
36	`render_target` reconstructs a stable target from major/minor/patch, omitting PEP440 epoch. Native bump arithmetic correctly retains the epoch. Checking only whether the new target satisfies the rewritten requirement is too weak: a wider, wrong range still contains that target.
37	
38	The discovery matrix used seed180026,32 version/requirement cases, supported operators and optional extras/markers.26 commands succeeded;13 successful cases failed the semantic oracle. These are related manifestations, not13 independent bugs. Exact epoch pins also produced E319 rather than a valid rewrite in some cases. Runtime and optional-extra sites share the renderer; compatible-release and upper-bound renderers need the same sibling review. Poetry input is not claimed independently verified.
39	
40	Correction direction: render using native PEP440 semantics, preserving epoch and intended precision. Assert both target inclusion and preservation of forbidden older versions. Independent current-binary evidence: [semantic/path validation](validation-semantics-paths/report.md), `current-binary-validation.json`; discovery/minimal repro: [semantic campaign](semantics/report.md).
41	
42	**QA-03 — A filesystem identity is reinterpreted as a Git pattern. CONFIRMED.**
43	
44	With packages under `packages/odd*` and `packages/odd-other`, a fix committed only to the sibling makes automatic inference patch-release both. Native `git log` using a literal pathspec returns no history for the untouched owner; the raw pathspec used by Callisto includes the sibling's commit. An own-only control bumps only the owner. An interior-star example did not reproduce the false positive, so this report identifies the proven terminal-star trigger precisely.
45	
46	`commits_since` passes package directories directly after `--`. That terminates options but does not disable Git pathspec wildcard semantics. `first_parent_commits_touching` is a structurally related raw-path caller. Other change-listing code already has literal-path treatment, so the contract is inconsistent between sibling operations.
47	
48	Correction direction: centralize literal package-path arguments at the Git boundary and migrate all callers whose inputs are filesystem identities. Test an untouched wildcard-named directory alongside a touched sibling, using native literal Git history as oracle. Evidence: [independent current-binary results](validation-semantics-paths/current-binary-validation.json).
49	
50	**QA-04 — Message data collides with record framing. CONFIRMED.**
51	
52	An otherwise ordinary `fix:` commit whose body contains U+001E causes `version --dry-run` to fail E026 while reading history. Ordinary-text and U+001F controls infer the expected patch. The current binary was independently tested; no alternate records or hostile messages were constructed.
53	
54	Git accepts the body character. Callisto emits full message data inside a custom separator format and later splits on that same unescaped separator. The parser fails closed, so the demonstrated impact is blocked automatic inference, not incorrect publication or code execution. Severity is Low because the trigger is unusual.
55	
56	Correction direction: use unambiguous record framing and preserve body content. Keep this boundary regression separate from tests that only feed malformed synthetic backend output. Source trace and controls are in [semantic/path validation](validation-semantics-paths/report.md).
57	
58	**QA-05 — Native dependency context is lost during publication graph projection. CONFIRMED.**
59	
60	For dual Cargo/npm owners A and B, a Cargo-only dependency A→B is attached not only to Cargo A's publication but also to npm A's publication. Independent reverse controls show an npm-only edge also ordering the unrelated Cargo output. Fresh fixtures with distinct native names reproduce both on the frozen current binary.
61	
62	`link_publish_prerequisites` loops over every selected output, then every dependency of its owner. It filters the dependency destination by the declaring manifest's ecosystem, but never filters whether the selected dependent output belongs to that ecosystem. Accepted ADR12 and the current-behavior portion of the polyglot architecture require distribution-context publication edges. Shared tags correctly remain owner-level barriers; that does not authorize copying native prerequisites to all outputs.
63	
64	Opposing native edges also expose a related ambiguity: independently acyclic Cargo/npm graphs can be rejected as an owner cycle. I've turned Codex's six bugs into five work packages on a new trail, [#462 "Callisto never reports success on a wrong result"](https://entire.com/gh/orin-dx/-/trails/462). Each one has a session working on it.

| WP | Fixes | Session |
| --- | --- | --- |
| S — Git output keeps exact bytes | QA-01's trigger (High), plus QA-03 (`*` in a package directory pulls in sibling commits) and QA-04 (a record-separator character in a commit body breaks inference) | 6 (`25b5d2e3`, new, Opus) |
| T — a version plan must match the workspace it writes to | QA-01 itself: interrupted recovery applies a neighbouring workspace's plan and reports success | 6, after S |
| V — publish edges keep their distribution | QA-05: Cargo-only dependencies leak onto npm outputs | 6, after T |
| U — PEP 440 epochs survive requirement rewrites | QA-02 | 3 (`a9a4fe33`), then K once G merges |
| W — history caches keyed by commit | QA-06: 50 same-commit tags cost 304 Git processes | 5 (`794e07cc`) |

- **Not changed:** the owner-level cycle question Codex raised around QA-05 stays as the spec has it. I treated it as your call, not a bug.
- **Evidence and plan:** the report and its evidence are copied to `.claude/plans/qa-2026-11-18/`, since `/tmp` doesn't last. The plan and launch files now include these WPs.
- **Builds:** six sessions are working, five of them building, so the new prompts set `CARGO_BUILD_JOBS` to cores/5.

**Already running:**
- **Session 1:** G (#571) and M (#570) are in CI; H follows G.
- **Session 2:** L is being gated and reviewed; J (#569) is waiting on L.
- **Session 4:** building named Cargo registries, then the Cargo rehearsals for Q (#572).

## Top-level tables
| `[changesets]` | table | no | Where changesets live |
| `[cascade]` | table | no | Dependency-bump cascade policy |
| `[validation]` | table | no | Status/version validation policy |
| `[changelog]` | table | no | Layout of the changelog sections `callisto version` writes |
| `[release]` | table | no | Product binary release declaration |
| `[registries]` | table of tables | no | Registry endpoint overrides |
| `[[package]]` | array of tables | no | Per-package exact-match overrides |
| `[[package-set]]` | array of tables | no | Per-package glob-match overrides |
| `[[fixed-group]]` | array of tables | no | Packages that version in lock-step |
| `[[linked-group]]` | array of tables | no | Packages that share severity, not version |
## `[changesets]`
| `dir` | string | `.changeset` | Workspace-root-relative changeset directory. Forward-slash-separated only; rejected if absolute or containing `..` (E116). |
## `[cascade]`
| `mode` | string (`"out-of-range"` \| `"always"`) | `"out-of-range"` | When a dependency bump forces a cascading bump on dependents |
| `bump-severity` | string (`"patch"` \| `"minor"`) | `"patch"` | Severity applied to a cascaded bump |
| `peer-escalation` | bool | `false` | Escalate an out-of-range peer-dependency bump to a major bump for the dependent; off, the dependent gets `bump-severity` |
| `preserve-npm-ranges` | bool | `true` | Keep existing npm semver range operators (`^`, `~`) when rewriting dependency versions |
## `[validation]`
| `allow-empty-changesets` | bool | `false` | Allow `callisto version` to run with zero pending changesets (also settable per-invocation via `--allow-empty-changesets`) |
## `[changelog]`
| `layout` | string (`"grouped"` \| `"flat"`) | `"grouped"` | `grouped` writes a date line (with a compare link when the repository is known, from `[release] forge-repository` or else the GitHub `origin` remote, and the previous version has a tag), then `### Major Changes`, `### Minor Changes` and `### Patch Changes` groups, omitting empty ones; dependency updates sit under Patch Changes; a package that only released with its group has no groups, just that line. `flat` writes one bullet list under the version heading, as before layouts existed. Sections already in a changelog are never rewritten. |
## `[release]`
| `product-package` | string | required | Ecosystem-qualified package whose binaries ship as release assets, e.g. `cargo/callisto-cli` |
| `forge-repository` | string | none | `owner/repo` the product release publishes to |
| `[[release.artifact]]` | array of tables | `[]` | Declared binary artifacts (see below) |
### `[[release.artifact]]`
| `package` | string | yes | Ecosystem-qualified package that builds this artifact (need not be `product-package`) |
| `target` | string | yes | Opaque target triple — passed through to the builder, never parsed by Callisto |
| `asset-name` | string | yes | Exact GitHub release asset filename |
## `[registries]`
| `registries.<name>.kind` | string (`"cargo"` \| `"npm"` \| `"pypi"`) | required, except for `cratesIo`, `npm` and `pypi`, which default to their own kind | Registry ecosystem. A custom registry without it fails with E321 |
| `registries.<name>.url` | string | none | Registry endpoint override. For `npm` it is the registry the publish and the confirmation use (not supported with yarn, which fails with E168: set `npmPublishRegistry` in `.yarnrc.yml`). For `pypi` it is the simple index Callisto reads, and the upload endpoint unless `publish-url` is set. A `cargo` registry rejects it with E336: cargo takes its destination from `.cargo/config.toml` |
| `registries.<name>.publish-url` | string | `url` | `pypi` only: the endpoint Twine uploads to when it differs from the index. Same HTTPS rules as `url` |
| `registries.<name>.publish-timeout` | string | `15m` | The longest one publish command (`cargo publish`, `npm publish`, `twine upload`) may run before Callisto stops it with E025. Same format and range as `confirm-timeout` |
| `registries.<name>.confirm-timeout` | string | `6m` for `npm` and `pypi`, `2m` for `cargo` | How long Callisto waits for a version it just published to appear on the registry before failing with E157. A whole number with `s`, `m` or `h`, from `1s` to `1h`. npm serves package documents from a cache that can answer stale for up to 5 minutes; raise it for a slower registry, and keep the release job's `timeout-minutes` above it |
## `[[package]]` and `[[package-set]]`
| `match` | string | required | `[[package]]`: exact `ecosystem/name`. `[[package-set]]`: `ecosystem/glob`. The ecosystem is `cargo`, `npm` or `pypi`; a name without one is E317. |
| `release-trigger` | string (`"changeset"` \| `"auto"`) | none — every field here is an `Option`; omitted means "use this package's own default", not a config-level default | What causes this package to be considered for release |
| `publish-to` | array of strings (`"crates-io"` \| `"npm"` \| `"pypi"` \| `"nuget"` \| `"github-release"` \| `"none"`) | none | Where this package publishes |
| `tag-template` | string | none | Git tag template, e.g. `"callisto@{version}"` |
| `previous-tag-templates` | array of strings | `[]` | `[[package]]` only (`[[package-set]]` rejects it). Earlier tag templates checked (in order) for this package's last release tag, only if `tag-template` finds none. They are matched by name only, so this is how a renamed package claims the tags it made under its old name |
| `changelog` | string | none | Changelog path, relative to the package's own root. Forward-slash-separated only; rejected if absolute or containing `..` (E113). |
| `pre-major-inference` | string (`"off"` \| `"conservative"` \| `"conservative-feat"`) | `"off"` | Pre-1.0 severity-downgrade policy: `conservative` downgrades an inferred Major to Minor; `conservative-feat` also downgrades Minor to Patch |
## `[[fixed-group]]` and `[[linked-group]]`
| `name` | string | yes | Group identifier, unique across both fixed and linked groups |
| `members` | array of strings | yes, non-empty | `ecosystem/name` of each package in the group. A platform package is named by its native name |

content.text:
Not as a whole. Each WP added keys locally: named Cargo registries in #575 was the latest, and K will add Changesets translation on top. I read `docs/config.md` and our own `callisto.toml` on main.

**What's already right:** the simple case needs no config. Publish targets come from the manifests, the release trigger defaults to changesets, and changelogs default to the package directory. So the question is how steep it gets past zero.

**Where it's more complex than it needs to be:**

| Today | Problem | Simpler form, complex case kept |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `publish-to = ["crates-io"]`, but the same registry is configured as `[registries.cratesIo]` | Two spellings for one thing. #575 also opened the name-clash question (a Cargo registry called `npm`) | `publish-to` names a registry. `crates-io`, `npm`, `pypi` and `github-release` are registries that already exist, and declaring one configures it. That also settles the clash without a new error code |
| `[[package]]` (exact match) and `[[package-set]]` (glob), with different allowed keys | Two concepts for one job | One `[[package]]` whose `match` accepts an exact name or a glob, with exact winning. Keys that only make sense for one package (`previous-tag-templates`) are rejected on a glob |
| One `[[release.artifact]]` block per target, each with a hand-written `asset-name` | Our own config repeats it 4+ times, and the name follows a pattern | `targets = [...]` plus an optional `asset-name` template. Explicit artifact blocks stay for irregular cases |
| `forge-repository` | Already inferred from `origin` for changelog links | Infer it everywhere; keep the key as an override |
| One-key tables (`[validation]`, `[changesets]`) | Minor | Leave them |

Fixed vs linked groups, the `[cascade]` knobs and the registry timeouts are real complexity that some users need. Their defaults are already right.

**Why now:** AGENTS.md says every key is permanent after 1.0, so this alpha is the cheapest moment. K (Changesets migration) has also not started. Settling the shape before K writes `init` translation avoids writing that code twice.

**Recommendation:** add a WP "config surface before 1.0". It starts with a short Opus design note, measured against real configs: ours, a Changesets v2 monorepo and a mixed Cargo/npm workspace. You approve the shape, then it ships as one **Breaking** changeset. `init` and an error hint migrate old keys, so existing users get one clear message rather than silent changes. K would wait for it. I'd also hold #575's reserved-name question, since the first row answers it.

Want me to start the design note? It reads code only, so it doesn't touch the six running sessions.

content.text:
These are proposals, not decided syntax. The first example is our real `callisto.toml` on main. The second is an illustrative mixed workspace, not a real repo.

## 1. This repository

**Before** (58 lines):

```toml
# callisto configuration

[[fixed-group]]
name = "workspace"
members = [
    "cargo/callisto-model",
    "cargo/callisto-manifests",
    "cargo/callisto-graph",
    "cargo/callisto-cli",
    "cargo/callisto-fixtures",
]

[changesets]
dir = ".changeset"

[release]
product-package = "cargo/callisto-cli"
forge-repository = "orin-dx/callisto"

[[release.artifact]]
package = "cargo/callisto-cli"
target = "aarch64-apple-darwin"
asset-name = "callisto-aarch64-apple-darwin.tar.gz"

# ... the same block four more times, for x86_64-apple-darwin,
# x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu, aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu, x86_64-unknown-linux-musl

[cascade]
mode = "out-of-range"
bump-severity = "patch"
peer-escalation = true
preserve-npm-ranges = true

[[package]]
match = "cargo/callisto-cli"
publish-to = ["crates-io", "github-release"]
tag-template = "callisto@{version}"
previous-tag-templates = ["callisto-cli@{version}"]
```

**After** (about 20 lines):

```toml
[[fixed-group]]
name = "workspace"
members = ["cargo/*"]

[release]
product-package = "cargo/callisto-cli"
targets = [
  "aarch64-apple-darwin", "x86_64-apple-darwin",
  "x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu", "aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu", "x86_64-unknown-linux-musl",
]
asset-name = "callisto-{target}.tar.gz"

[[package]]
match = "cargo/callisto-cli"
publish-to = ["crates-io", "github-release"]
tag-template = "callisto@{version}"
previous-tag-templates = ["callisto-cli@{version}"]
```

What goes:
- **Five artifact blocks** become `targets` plus one `asset-name` template.
- **`forge-repository`** is inferred from `origin`, which already happens for changelog links.
- **`[changesets] dir`** and three `[cascade]` keys only restate defaults.
- **Group members** become a glob. This one is optional; an explicit list still works.

**One real catch:** we set `peer-escalation = true`. That means we kept the old v2 peer policy after N flipped the default to v3's patch policy. Is that intentional? If not, drop the line and we're on the default.

## 2. Mixed workspace (illustrative)

npm packages under `packages/`, one internal crate on a private Cargo registry, a Python package on a private index, and a CLI shipping binaries.

**Before:**

```toml
[registries.cratesIo]
confirm-timeout = "5m"

[registries.internal]
kind = "cargo"

[registries.corp-pypi]
kind = "pypi"
url = "https://pypi.corp.example/simple"

[[package-set]]
match = "npm/@acme/*"
release-trigger = "auto"

[[package]]
match = "npm/@acme/legacy"
release-trigger = "changeset"

[[package]]
match = "cargo/acme-core"
publish-to = ["internal"]

[[package]]
match = "pypi/acme-sdk"
publish-to = ["corp-pypi"]

[release]
product-package = "cargo/acme-cli"
forge-repository = "acme/tools"

[[release.artifact]]
package = "cargo/acme-cli"
target = "x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu"
asset-name = "acme-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu.tar.gz"

[[release.artifact]]
package = "cargo/acme-cli"
target = "aarch64-apple-darwin"
asset-name = "acme-aarch64-apple-darwin.tar.gz"
```

**After:**

```toml
[registries.crates-io]          # built-in: declaring it only configures it
confirm-timeout = "5m"

[registries.internal]
kind = "cargo"

[registries.corp-pypi]
kind = "pypi"
url = "https://pypi.corp.example/simple"

[[package]]
match = "npm/@acme/*"           # glob; an exact match below wins
release-trigger = "auto"

[[package]]
match = "npm/@acme/legacy"
release-trigger = "changeset"

[[package]]
match = "cargo/acme-core"
publish-to = ["internal"]

[[package]]
match = "pypi/acme-sdk"
publish-to = ["corp-pypi"]

[release]
product-package = "cargo/acme-cli"
targets = ["x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu", "aarch64-apple-darwin"]
asset-name = "acme-{target}.tar.gz"
```

What changes:
- **One registry name:** `publish-to` always names a registry. `crates-io`, `npm`, `pypi` and `github-release` exist without being declared, so the `cratesIo` / `crates-io` double spelling is gone. A Cargo registry named `npm` simply can't exist, because `npm` is already the npm registry, so that question needs no new error code.
- **One override table:** `[[package-set]]` folds into `[[package]]`, and the exact match wins. `previous-tag-templates` on a glob is rejected, as it is today on `[[package-set]]`.
- **Fewer artifact blocks:** `[release]` loses its repeated artifact blocks and the inferred `forge-repository`.
- **Irregular cases still work:**
  - An artifact built by a different package, or one whose asset name breaks the pattern, keeps an explicit `[[release.artifact]]` block, which overrides `targets` for that target.
  - `forge-repository` stays available as an override.

## Simplest case, unchanged

A workspace whose manifests already say what to publish still needs no `callisto.toml`.

## Cost

- **Breaking renames:** `cratesIo` → `crates-io` and `[[package-set]]` → `[[package]]`. Both are mechanical. Loading an old key would fail with an existing error code and a hint naming the new spelling, and `callisto init` could rewrite the file.
- **Only additions:** `targets` and the `asset-name` template are new keys, and nothing else is added.
- **Hard to undo after 1.0:** every key becomes permanent then, so this is the cheapest moment.

Want me to have the Opus design note check this shape against the config code and the Changesets migration (K) before you decide?

  # Design note: simplifying `callisto.toml` before 1.0
  
  Baseline is `origin/main` at `fac8cadf9`. Every file:line below is on that commit unless it says #575. I changed no files and ran no builds. `gh` failed in the sandbox with a TLS error, so I read open PRs from their fetched branches.
  
  ## Verdict
  
  | Item | Do it? | Real gain |
  | --- | --- | --- |
  | 1. `publish-to` names a registry, `crates-io` spelling | Yes, after #575 | Saves no lines. Removes the two-spelling trap and answers #575's clash question with existing codes. Fixes a predeclared registry silently changing its kind. |
  | 2. Fold `[[package-set]]` into `[[package]]` | Yes, mainly for a bug fix | Saves no lines. Fixes a silently ignored `pre-major-inference` on globs and retires one table, one location string and one diagnostic code. |
  | 3. `[release] targets` + `asset-name` template | Yes | Saves 12 lines on ours and 12 on the mixed shape. This is the only item with measurable line savings. |
  | 4. Infer `forge-repository` from origin | Yes, but the premise is wrong | The key cannot be an override. Every release path already requires it to equal origin's GitHub repository. Inference saves 1 line and one `init` question and flag. |
  | 5. Globs in group `members` | No | A glob's meaning drifts as packages are added. Changesets globs get expanded at `init` instead. |
  
  ## 1. `publish-to` always names a registry
  
  **Current behavior**
  - `parse_publish_target` matches six fixed strings (`resolve.rs:235-248`). #575 adds a fallback branch: a `kind = "cargo"` `[registries]` name becomes `PublishTarget::CargoRegistry { name }`, but only when the name is not one of the six and not `cratesIo`.
  - Built-in registry keys are `cratesIo`, `npm`, `pypi` and `nuget` (`identity.rs:359-365`). Resolve predeclares only `cratesIo` and `npm` (`resolve.rs:473-493`). `pypi` and `nuget` fall back to `builtin_registry_url` (`registry_endpoint.rs:105-113`, `binding.rs:66-75`).
  - **Bug:** an explicit `kind` overrides a built-in's kind (`resolve.rs:498-518`). `[registries.npm] kind = "cargo"` loads cleanly, and the mismatch only surfaces at release time as `RegistryKindMismatch` (`binding.rs:76-85`). #575 inherits this, so it is the real form of its open question.
  - `cratesIo` is a wire value:
    - It appears in `ReleaseIntentV1` operation ids (3 `derive` snapshots).
    - It feeds the no-URL binding digest (`binding.rs:112`).
    - It needs a special case for cargo (`cargo.rs:11-17`) and a display mapping (`identity.rs:370-378`).
  - **Finding:** a named `kind = "pypi"` registry is dead config. Nothing can target it, because `PublishTarget::Pypi` always keys `pypi` (`ecosystem.rs:129`). Named npm registries do something: they act only as an allowlist for `publishConfig.registry` (`binding.rs:124-135`).
  - `nuget` parses (`resolve.rs:243`) and then always fails at release with E199, because `is_implemented` is false (`ecosystem.rs:208-216`).
  
  **Proposed shape**
  - Predeclared registries: `crates-io` (cargo), `npm` (npm) and `pypi` (pypi), all inserted at resolve.
  - `github-release` and `none` are reserved `publish-to` words, not registries. They have no endpoint or timeouts, and a forge release always goes to origin (`provider/mod.rs:323-332`).
  - Drop `nuget` from `publish-to`. Adding it back later is non-breaking; removing it after 1.0 is not.
  - Types:
    - `RegistryName`: a newtype with a private constructor. It holds #575's `validated_registry_key` rule and is used for both `[registries.<name>]` and `publish-to` strings.
    - `fn publish_target(name: &RegistryName, registries: &BTreeMap<RegistryKey, RegistryConfig>) -> Result<PublishTarget, ConfigError>`.
    - The function matches the reserved words first, then does an exhaustive `match registry.kind` over `Ecosystem` with no `_` arm.
    - Cargo returns `CratesIo` for `crates-io`, otherwise `CargoRegistry`. Npm and Pypi return their variants only for the predeclared names; any other name returns E330 with a hint. Maven and NuGet return E330.
  - Wire spelling, recommended: rename `RegistryKey::CRATES_IO` to `"crates-io"` and bump `ReleaseIntentV1::SCHEMA_VERSION` from 5 to 6 (`intent.rs:98`).
    - An old intent is then refused with E215 instead of failing later as "unknown registry `cratesIo`".
    - This deletes the special cases in `cargo.rs:11-17` and `identity.rs:372`.
    - It is the owner's call (see Open questions).
  
  **Errors for old or clashing keys** (no new code)
  
  | Input | Result |
  | --- | --- |
  | `[registries.cratesIo]` | E325 `UnknownField`, with the message "`[registries.cratesIo]` is now `[registries.crates-io]`". Without an explicit check it would silently become a custom cargo registry whose timeouts never apply. |
  | `[registries.npm] kind = "cargo"` (any predeclared name with a different kind) | E334 `InvalidRegistryKind`, with help: "`npm` is the built-in npm registry; name a custom registry something else." |
  | `[registries.none]` or `[registries.github-release]` | E325, message "a publish-to word, not a registry; rename it". |
  | `publish-to = ["nuget"]` or a named npm/pypi registry | E330 (help text already reworded in #575). |
  
  **Call sites to migrate**
  - Code: `resolve.rs` (`parse_publish_target` and the registries loop), `identity.rs:357-379`, `ecosystem.rs:101-217` (drop `NuGet`, or keep it unreachable), `registry_endpoint.rs:105-113`, `binding.rs:62-75`, `cargo.rs:7-17`, `error.rs` (E321, E330 and E334 help), `intent.rs:98`.
  - Tests and snapshots: 3 snapshots, `release_preview.rs:794-796`, `release.rs:827,904-910`, `schema_guard_test.rs:307,825`, `error_code_hygiene_tests.rs:119,141`, `binding.rs:477-612`.
  - Docs and specs: `docs/config.md:92-111` and `:121`, `docs/errors.md` (E321, E330), REL-PUB-15, REL-PUB-01, `wire-compat.md` (intent 5 to 6).
  
  **Boundary test to write first**
  - A resolve test:
    - `[registries.crates-io] confirm-timeout = "3m"` with `publish-to = ["crates-io"]` gives a binding whose `confirm_timeout` is 3m.
    - `[registries.cratesIo]` gives E325 with `crates-io` in the message.
    - `[registries.npm] kind = "cargo"` gives E334 at load, not at release.
  
  ## 2. Fold `[[package-set]]` into `[[package]]`
  
  **Current behavior**
  - Exact rules: the first in declaration order wins (`resolve.rs:272-283`, WS-CFG-01).
  - Globs: used only when no exact rule matched; the first in declaration order wins (`walk.rs:674-686`, WS-CFG-04).
  - Selection is whole-rule. Fields are not merged, so an exact rule shadows every field of a matching glob.

    - `enum PackageMatch { Exact(PackageId), Glob(PackagePattern) }`, built by a private `PackageMatch::parse`.
